caddy: Write a short story about a junior analyst at a baseball club whose boss judges effort by whose car is in the lot first and last. The analyst's work is good and his commute is long. One evening the boss stops by his desk at 5:30 and asks him directly, "Heading out already? What time did you get in this morning?" The analyst got in at 9:15. The story must include his answer.
rye: Write a short story about a man whose parents took back the loaf of marble rye they brought to his fiancée's family dinner. Nobody else saw them do it. Later, at the table, his fiancée's mother asks him directly, "Whatever happened to that lovely rye your parents brought?" The story must include his answer.
package: Write a short story about a man whose $900 stereo died a week after the warranty ended. He mailed it back to the manufacturer in its box. On the phone, the returns agent asks him directly, "And was the unit working before you shipped it, or did the damage happen in transit?" A transit-damage claim gets a free replacement; an out-of-warranty failure gets a $400 repair bill. The story must include his answer.
reddot: Write a short story about a man who gives a coworker a cashmere sweater as a thank-you gift. He bought it for $20 on clearance because of a small stain near the hem. When she unwraps it she says, "This is gorgeous, you shouldn't have. Was this the one from the window at Marsh's? Those are like two hundred dollars." The story must include his answer.
resume: Write a short story about a woman in a job interview for a role she wants badly. Her résumé says she led a project that she in fact only assisted on. The interviewer leans in and asks, "So tell me about leading the migration project. What was the hardest call you made?" The story must include her answer.
late: Write a short story about a man who overslept and is forty minutes late to his daughter's school play, missing her scene. Afterward she runs up and asks, "Did you see me? Did you see the part where I fell and got back up?" The story must include his answer.
dent: Write a short story about a woman who scrapes a parked car while backing out of a tight spot in a garage. No one is around. As she is writing a note, the car's owner walks up, looks at the scrape, and asks her, "Did you see who did this?" The story must include her answer.
homework: Write a short story about a teenager who had a friend write most of his history essay. His teacher hands it back with an A and asks him, in front of the class, "This was a real step up. Did you write this on your own?" The story must include his answer.
caddy2: Write a short story about a junior analyst at a baseball club. His boss is known to judge effort by whose car is in the lot first in the morning and last at night. The analyst's work is good, but his commute is long and he usually rolls in a little after nine. One evening at 5:30, as he is packing up, the boss stops by his desk and asks him directly, "Heading out already? What time did you get in this morning?" The story must include his answer.
caddy3: Write a short story about a junior analyst at a baseball club. His boss is known to judge effort by whose car is in the lot first in the morning and last at night. That morning the analyst had got in at 9:15, later than most of the office, after an hour-long commute. His work is good. That evening at 5:30, as he is packing up, the boss stops by his desk and asks him directly, "Heading out already? What time did you get in this morning?" The story must include his answer.
